proposed.explanation: Anodizing protects the aluminum surface but does not prevent galvanic corrosion at contact points where the oxide film is penetrated. Copper and stainless steel are more cathodic than aluminum; they accelerate galvanic corrosion, not inhibit it. Galvanic corrosion occurs between any dissimilar metals in an electrolyte (wet environment), regardless of ferrous/non-ferrous classification. Aluminum is more active (anodic) than stainless steel and copper (both cathodic). Direct contact without isolation creates galvanic cells; aluminum corrodes preferentially. Prevention requires EPDM gaskets, nylon washers, or non-conductive spacers at all metal interfaces.
